set.stimulus:
Ten persons sit in two parallel rows of five persons each, with equal distance between adjacent persons. Persons in Row 1 face south and persons in Row 2 face north, so each person in Row 1 faces a person in Row 2. Q, R, S, T and U sit in Row 1, and A, B, C, D and E sit in Row 2, not necessarily in the same order. Left and right are taken from each person's own point of view.

1. E sits to the immediate left of C.
2. C sits third to the right of A.
3. B sits second to the right of E.
4. U sits to the immediate right of S.
5. Only three persons sit between R and U.
6. Only one person sits between U and Q.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Who sits second to the right of E?

steps: Start with clues 1, 2 and 3: together they fix C, E, A and B.
Clue 5 gives 2 cases — Case 1: R facing A and U facing B; Case 2: R second to the left of Q and U second to the right of Q.
Clue 4 cannot be met in Case 1, so it is rejected.
Clues 4 and 6 then place S and Q.
T takes the only seat left.
D takes the only seat left.
The chain fits into the row in only one way.
Final arrangement (west to east): Row 1 — U, S, Q, T, R; Row 2 — A, D, E, C, B.
E faces north, so E's right is towards the east end.
Second to the right of E: C → B — answer **B**.
solution.shortcut: Take left/right from the person’s own facing, then count seats along the row.
solution.trap: A is second to the left — counting in the wrong direction gives this option.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: What is the position of U with respect to R?

steps: Start with clues 1, 2 and 3: together they fix C, E, A and B.
Clue 5 gives 2 cases — Case 1: R facing A and U facing B; Case 2: R second to the left of Q and U second to the right of Q.
Clue 4 cannot be met in Case 1, so it is rejected.
Clues 4 and 6 then place S and Q.
T takes the only seat left.
D takes the only seat left.
The chain fits into the row in only one way.
Final arrangement (west to east): Row 1 — U, S, Q, T, R; Row 2 — A, D, E, C, B.
R faces south, so R's right is towards the west end.
From R, going to R's right: T → Q → S → U — **Fourth to the right**.
solution.shortcut: Stand in the seat of the second person, face where they face, and count.
solution.trap: Fourth to the left is what you get by taking left/right from your own view instead of R's.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: If T and S interchange their seats, who will sit second to the right of S?

steps: Start with clues 1, 2 and 3: together they fix C, E, A and B.
Clue 5 gives 2 cases — Case 1: R facing A and U facing B; Case 2: R second to the left of Q and U second to the right of Q.
Clue 4 cannot be met in Case 1, so it is rejected.
Clues 4 and 6 then place S and Q.
T takes the only seat left.
D takes the only seat left.
The chain fits into the row in only one way.
Final arrangement (west to east): Row 1 — U, S, Q, T, R; Row 2 — A, D, E, C, B.
After the interchange S takes T's seat (and its facing).
Second to the right of S now: Q → T — **T**.
solution.shortcut: Swap the two names on your diagram first; then count from the new seat.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Four of the following five pairs are alike in a certain way based on the given arrangement and so form a group. Which pair does not belong to that group?

steps: Start with clues 1, 2 and 3: together they fix C, E, A and B.
Clue 5 gives 2 cases — Case 1: R facing A and U facing B; Case 2: R second to the left of Q and U second to the right of Q.
Clue 4 cannot be met in Case 1, so it is rejected.
Clues 4 and 6 then place S and Q.
T takes the only seat left.
D takes the only seat left.
The chain fits into the row in only one way.
Final arrangement (west to east): Row 1 — U, S, Q, T, R; Row 2 — A, D, E, C, B.
In "A, C", "D, B", "R, S" and "T, U", the second person sits third to the right of the first.
In "E, B", B sits second to the right of E — so **E, B** is the odd one.
solution.shortcut: Find the relation in the first two pairs (same direction, same count), then test the rest.
solution.trap: Check direction from the first person’s own facing — a pair that is the same distance but on the other side does not belong.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true according to the given arrangement?
options: B is an immediate neighbour of A
D sits to the immediate right of E
D sits to the immediate left of E
E sits second to the left of C
C sits to the immediate right of B

steps: Start with clues 1, 2 and 3: together they fix C, E, A and B.
Clue 5 gives 2 cases — Case 1: R facing A and U facing B; Case 2: R second to the left of Q and U second to the right of Q.
Clue 4 cannot be met in Case 1, so it is rejected.
Clues 4 and 6 then place S and Q.
T takes the only seat left.
D takes the only seat left.
The chain fits into the row in only one way.
Final arrangement (west to east): Row 1 — U, S, Q, T, R; Row 2 — A, D, E, C, B.
(A) B is an immediate neighbour of A — false.
(B) D sits to the immediate right of E — false.
(C) D sits to the immediate left of E — **true**.
(D) E sits second to the left of C — false.
(E) C sits to the immediate right of B — false.
solution.shortcut: Test each statement on the final diagram, not on the clue list.
solution.trap: A statement copied from a clue with one word changed (left ↔ right, second ↔ third) looks familiar but is wrong.

set.subject: reasoning
set.title: Parallel rows
set.stimulus:
Ten persons sit in two parallel rows of five persons each, with equal distance between adjacent persons. Persons in Row 1 face south and persons in Row 2 face north, so each person in Row 1 faces a person in Row 2. L, M, N, P and Q sit in Row 1, and A, B, C, D and E sit in Row 2, not necessarily in the same order. Left and right are taken from each person's own point of view.

1. Q faces C.
2. Neither L nor A is an immediate neighbour of N.
3. E sits to the immediate left of C.
4. Q sits second to the right of N.
5. Q sits to the immediate right of M.
6. D sits to the immediate left of A.
7. C is not an immediate neighbour of D.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Who faces N?

steps: Start with clues 1, 3, 4 and 5: together they fix Q, C, E, N and M.
Clue 6 gives 2 cases — Case 1: A facing N and D facing M; Case 2: A facing P and D facing N.
Clue 7 rules out Case 1 — only Case 2 survives.
Clue 2 then places L.
P takes the only seat left.
B takes the only seat left.
The chain fits into the row in only one way.
Final arrangement (west to east): Row 1 — L, Q, M, N, P; Row 2 — E, C, B, D, A.
In the same column of the other row as N sits **D**.
solution.shortcut: The person in the same column of the other row.

questions.prompt: Who are the immediate neighbours of Q?

steps: Start with clues 1, 3, 4 and 5: together they fix Q, C, E, N and M.

B takes the only seat left.
The chain fits into the row in only one way.
Final arrangement (west to east): Row 1 — L, Q, M, N, P; Row 2 — E, C, B, D, A.
On either side of Q sit M and L — **L and M**.
solution.shortcut: Read the two seats next to the person straight off the final diagram.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: If N and C interchange their seats, who will sit to the immediate left of C?

steps: Start with clues 1, 3, 4 and 5: together they fix Q, C, E, N and M.
Clue 6 gives 2 cases — Case 1: A facing N and D facing M; Case 2: A facing P and D facing N.

Immediately to the left of C now: P — **P**.
solution.shortcut: Swap the two names on your diagram first; then count from the new seat.
solution.trap: E is the answer before the interchange.
